info.title: Nexalware API
info.description: Nexalware is infrastructure for AI agents, and the software you write yourself, to act in the physical world. This is the HTTP API behind it: control physical devices and read their telemetry. Endpoints are grouped by who can call them: "Authentication" logs an existing account in and returns a session token; "Device Control" and "Schedules" work with an API key (scoped by a DeviceGrant); everything else manages dashboard resources (rules, grants, keys, devices, command catalogs) and is meant for the Nexalware web app itself, not third-party automation.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: A secret API key created on the dashboard (API Keys page). By itself it grants nothing - it must also have a DeviceGrant scoping it to the specific device(s) and command(s) it may call.

sessionAuth.description: A session token for an existing account, obtained from POST /auth/login (see the Authentication endpoints) - not an API key. Endpoints marked with this scheme reject API key callers outright, regardless of what that key is granted. Outside the Authentication endpoints themselves, everything requiring this scheme manages dashboard resources (rules, grants, keys, device configuration, command catalogs) and mirrors what a human does in the Nexalware web app - it is not meant to be automated by a third-party integration the way the Device Control and Schedules endpoints are.

details.description: Present only on request-body validation failures (400 Validation error).

refreshToken.description: Long-lived (30 days). Exchange it for a new pair at /auth/refresh instead of asking the user to log in again.

paramsSchema.description: JSON Schema for this command's params, or null if it takes none.

value.description: Numeric reading, null if this point only carried valueText.

valueText.description: Non-numeric reading (e.g. a status string), null if this point only carried a numeric value.

command.description: A command name from the device's catalog.

params.description: Only if that command declares a paramsSchema.

status.description: PENDING = created, not yet due. ACTIVE = onTs has passed, offTs has not. COMPLETED = offTs has passed. CANCELLED = deleted before completing.

metric.description: A telemetry metric this device has reported - see GET .../rules/context for the actual list.

keyId.description: An existing, enabled API key's keyId - the exact same value GET /api/v1/keys returns for that key, not the raw secret value. The webhook inherits exactly what that key's DeviceGrants already cover; there's no separate scope to set here.

An existing, enabled API key's keyId - the exact same value GET /api/v1/keys returns for that key, not the raw secret value. The webhook inherits exactly what that key's DeviceGrants already cover; there's no separate scope to set here.

url.description: Must use https:// - plain http:// is rejected. Nexalware POSTs every event visible to keyId here.

eventType.description: e.g. DEVICE_ONLINE, DEVICE_OFFLINE, RELAY_ON, RELAY_OFF, COMMAND_SENT, UNAUTHORIZED_ATTEMPT, SCHEDULE_CANCELLED.

source.description: What triggered this event, lowercased: "schedule", "user" (a dashboard session or API key), "device", "system", or "rule".

externalId.description: Whatever identifier the master itself assigns or discovers this sub-device by - the master's own concern, not Nexalware's.

capabilities.description: Whatever this sub-device's own `describe()` reported - Nexalware never assumes a shape in advance.

post.summary: Log in and obtain a session token
post.description: Exchanges an existing account's email/password for a token pair. This is how a third-party client (your own app, a custom login screen, a CLI) authenticates a user directly, without going through the Nexalware dashboard UI. Creating a *new* account is dashboard-only (nexalware.com/sign-up) and is not exposed here - this endpoint only signs in an account that already exists.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new session
post.description: Call this when the access token expires (every 15 minutes) rather than asking the user to log in again. The refresh token itself rotates on every use - store the new one.

post.summary: Revoke a refresh token
post.description: Invalidates the given refresh token so it can no longer be exchanged for new sessions. The current access token stays valid until its own 15-minute expiry - this only prevents renewing it.

get.summary: Get the logged-in user and account

post.summary: Request a one-time code to change your password
post.description: Emails a 6-digit code to the logged-in user, valid briefly. Submit it to `/auth/change-password` along with the new password. Requires an existing session (log in first) and an Admin or Owner role - a Member/Viewer session gets a 403 here.

429.description: A code was already sent recently

post.summary: Change your password
post.description: Finishes the flow started by `/auth/password/request-otp` - same session and role requirement applies. This changes the password for the currently logged-in user; it is not a "forgot password while logged out" flow.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

get.description: A dashboard session sees every device on the account. An API key only sees devices its own DeviceGrants actually cover (a direct device grant, or a project-level grant covering everything in that project) - the same scoping every command call is checked against, applied here too so a key never enumerates devices it has no access to. This is the right first call for an agent (SDK or the MCP server's `list_devices` tool) to make: discover which devices this key can act on before calling anything else.

post.summary: Register a new device
post.description: Creates the device record in a PENDING state with no MQTT credentials yet call "Generate credentials" separately before it can connect. This is a dashboard/session action, a human registering a device, not something an API key does.

name.description: Shown on the dashboard and in device lists.

boardType.description: Free text - whatever board this is, e.g. "esp32", "esp8266", "raspberry-pi". Not validated against a fixed list; see GET /catalog/boards for common values to offer in a picker.

appType.description: Free text - the application/industry this device is used for. See GET /catalog/apps for common values to offer in a picker.

appTypeOther.description: Only used when appType is "Custom" - the free-text value to show instead.

projectId.description: Groups this device under an existing project. Omit to leave it ungrouped, or to fall back to the account's default project if one exists.

description.example: Controls the light above the garage door.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

projectId.description: Move this device into a different project.

delete.description: Also deletes its schedules, rules, grants, telemetry, and approval history.

get.description: The commands this specific device supports right now what a control UI or an AI agent should present as its available actions. Devices with no custom DeviceType return the legacy ON/OFF/TOGGLE/STATUS set.

post.summary: Define a custom command for a device
post.description: Adds one command to this device's catalog (creating the catalog on first use). Once defined, any caller with a DeviceGrant covering this device can send it via POST /devices/{deviceId}/command.

name.description: The exact string clients will pass as `cmd` when sending this command. SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, must be unique per device type.

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the dashboard.

description.example: Sets the light to a specific brightness level.

kind.description: "ACTION" changes device state (e.g. turning something on). "QUERY" only reads it. Rules and schedules can only use ACTION commands.

paramsSchema.description: A JSON Schema describing what `params` a caller must send with this command. Leave null/omitted for a command that takes no arguments.

shape.description: How the dashboard renders this command as a control, purely cosmetic, has no effect on validation.

requiresApproval.description: If true, calling this command never executes immediately, it always creates a pending approval (202 response) for an Owner/Admin to confirm first. Also means it can never be used in a rule or schedule, both fire unattended.

post.summary: Send a command to a device
post.description:
The general-purpose command endpoint - validates the command and its params against the device's catalog, checks the caller's DeviceGrant, then either publishes it over MQTT immediately or (for a command marked `requiresApproval`) creates a pending approval instead of executing it. An API key needs a DeviceGrant covering this device and this command name - see the Authentication & Access guide.

**How to use this:** first call `GET /devices/{deviceId}/commands` to see exactly which `cmd` values this device accepts and what `params` (if any) each one expects, then send one of those `cmd` names here. A plain relay with no custom command catalog accepts `"ON"`, `"OFF"`, `"TOGGLE"`, and `"STATUS"` with no `params` at all.

cmd.description: A command name from this device's catalog - see GET /devices/{deviceId}/commands for the exact names this specific device accepts. Devices with no custom command catalog accept the legacy "ON"/"OFF"/"TOGGLE"/"STATUS" set.

params.description: Only include this if the command you're sending declares a paramsSchema in its catalog entry (e.g. SET_BRIGHTNESS might expect { "level": 60 }). Omit entirely for a command that takes no arguments, like plain ON/OFF.

queuedAt.description: Unix milliseconds. Optional - set this if your own app queued this command locally (e.g. while offline) before actually sending it, so Nexalware can reject it with COMMAND_EXPIRED if it sat for more than 5 minutes, instead of firing a stale command late. Omit it for a command sent immediately - it is never required.

target.description: Only set this if this device is a "master" orchestrating other physical devices locally (see the Device Orchestration docs) and you want to command one specific sub-device instead of the master itself. Omit for a normal command aimed at this device.

202.description: Command requires approval - pending an Owner/Admin decision, not yet sent

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

post.summary: Shorthand for sending the ON command

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

post.summary: Shorthand for sending the OFF command

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

post.summary: Interpret free text into a command and send it
post.description: Runs `text` against this device's (or, with `target` set, a sub-device's) own command catalog through an LLM, then dispatches whatever command it resolves through the exact same path `POST .../command` uses - same DeviceGrant check, same approval flow, same everything. If the text doesn't clearly resolve to one catalog command, nothing is sent - the response comes back with `ok: false` and a `reply` you can show the caller instead. Meant for building a chat-style interface on top of the API; the strict/structured way to send a command is still `POST .../command`.

text.description: Free-text instruction, interpreted against this device's (or sub-device's, if target is set) own command catalog. Not guaranteed to resolve - see the response's "reply" and "interpreted" fields.
text.example: turn the porch light on and dim it to half

target.description: A sub-device ID behind this device to interpret and dispatch against instead of the device itself.

200.description: Either the command was sent, or nothing matched clearly enough to act on

reply.description: A short natural-language message to show the user.

value.reply: I couldn't find a command for that on this device.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

502.description: The NLP provider is unreachable or not configured

post.summary: Revoke a device's credentials
Generate MQTT credentials for a device
post.description: Firmware-facing credentials for connecting to the MQTT broker - not the same thing as an API key. The password is shown once and is not recoverable afterward; use "Reveal credentials" only re-shows what was already generated.

200.description: OK, save the password now, it will not be shown again in this form

post.summary: Re-show a device's existing MQTT credentials
post.description: Step-up protected - requires re-confirming your account password. Every call is written to the device's audit log.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

get.description:
Time-series readings this device has reported, newest first, what an AI agent needs to learn patterns rather than only react to the latest value.

**Example:** `GET /devices/dev_a1b2c3/telemetry?metric=temperature&limit=50` returns the last 50 temperature readings. Omit `metric` to get every metric this device reports, mixed together in one list.

schema.description: Only return readings for this metric name, omit to get every metric this device reports.
Max rows to return, 1-1000. Defaults to 100.
Unix milliseconds - only return readings recorded at or after this time. Omit for no lower bound.

get.summary: Read the most recent value per telemetry metric
get.description: The quickest "current state" snapshot - one row per metric this device has ever reported, plus its relay state. Use this instead of `/telemetry` when you just need "what is this device's situation right now", not history.

state.description: The device's free-form current-state snapshot, whatever shape its firmware last published, or null if it never has.

relayState.description: Legacy ON/OFF relay state, null for devices that don't use the simple relay model.

get.description: Static reference data no authentication required. Used to populate the "board type" picker when registering a device - `boardType` in POST /devices/register is free text, this is just suggestions, not an enforced list.

example.name: ESP32
example.description: Wi-Fi + Bluetooth, the most common choice.

get.description: Static reference data no authentication required. Same idea as /catalog/boards, but for `appType` when registering a device.
Schedules that are PENDING (created, not due yet) or ACTIVE (currently running). For schedules that already finished or were cancelled, see GET .../schedules/history instead.

post.summary: Create or replace a schedule slot
post.description: A device has up to 5 slots (0-4). `onCommand`/`offCommand` default to plain ON/OFF; any other command still fires reliably from the server at the scheduled time, but only the plain ON/OFF case also syncs to firmware for offline self-execution. An API key needs a DeviceGrant covering both commands used, exactly like sending them directly with POST .../command.

slot.description: Which of the device's 5 schedule slots (0-4) to use. Creating a schedule in an already-used slot replaces it.

onTs.description: Unix seconds - when to fire onCommand.

offTs.description: Unix seconds - when to fire offCommand.

label.description: Short label shown on the dashboard, max 7 characters.

onCommand.description: Defaults to { command: "ON" } if omitted. Must be a command from the device's catalog (see GET /devices/{deviceId}/commands) that does not require approval.

offCommand.description: Defaults to { command: "OFF" } if omitted. Same rules as onCommand.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

get.summary: Get the command choices available for scheduling
get.description: The same command catalog GET /devices/{deviceId}/commands returns, filtered to commands a schedule can actually use (kind ACTION only, a schedule can't "run" a QUERY command). Use this to populate a command picker before calling POST .../schedules.

put.description: Only the fields provided are changed, everything else on the existing schedule stays as-is.

onTs.description: Unix seconds. Omit to leave unchanged.

offTs.description: Unix seconds. Omit to leave unchanged.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it
Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

get.description: Most recent first, capped at the last 50.

post.summary: Create a rule
post.description: Runs continuously: whenever a matching telemetry point arrives, every condition is checked (all must pass), and if they do, `action` fires automatically, no human involved. A rule condition can only reference a telemetry metric this device has already reported at least once - check GET .../rules/context first. The action command is checked the same way an unattended schedule action is - commands marked `requiresApproval` cannot be used here.

get.summary: Get the metrics and commands available for building a rule
get.description: The telemetry metrics this device has actually reported (only these can be used in a condition) and its command catalog (only ACTION commands not marked requiresApproval can be used as the rule's action). Use this to populate a rule builder UI before calling POST .../rules.
Includes grants scoped directly to this device, grants scoped to its whole project, and grants scoped to one sub-device behind it - all three apply.

post.summary: Grant an API key or team member access to a device
post.description: This is how an API key gets permission to call device commands it has none by default. Provide exactly one of `apiKeyId` or `membershipId`. Add `subDeviceId` to narrow the grant to one sub-device behind this device (an orchestrator "master") instead of the whole device - omit it to reach every sub-device behind the device, same as today. Requires an Owner or Admin session; API keys cannot create grants for themselves or anyone else.

apiKeyId.description: Grant an API key access. Provide exactly one of apiKeyId or membershipId, never both.

membershipId.description: Grant a team member access (rarely needed - Owners/Admins already have full access, this is for scoping a Member/Viewer). Provide exactly one of apiKeyId or membershipId.

subDeviceId.description: Narrow the grant to one sub-device behind this device instead of the whole device. Omit to reach every sub-device behind it too.

commands.description: Which command names this grant allows, matching the names from GET /devices/{deviceId}/commands. Use ["*"] to allow every command.

scope.description: READ = can read state/telemetry only, ACTION commands are rejected even if listed. WRITE = can also send the listed ACTION commands. FULL = WRITE plus dashboard-adjacent reads. Most integrations want WRITE.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601. Omit or null for a grant that never expires.

activeDays.description: 0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday. Omit for every day.

activeFromMinute.description: Minutes since midnight UTC (480 = 8:00 AM). Pair with activeToMinute for a time-of-day window, e.g. business hours only.

rateLimitPerMinute.description: Max commands per minute this grant allows. Omit for no extra limit beyond the account's own.

get.description: Never includes the raw secret, only `prefix` (e.g. `nxw_live_sk_ab12`) to help you tell keys apart, the full value is shown exactly once, at creation.

post.summary: Create an API key
post.description:
The raw key is returned once, at creation only, and cannot be recovered afterward. A new key can call nothing until a DeviceGrant is created for it (see the Grants endpoints).

**Next step:** copy the `key` value from the response (starts with `nxw_live_sk_`), then call POST /devices/{deviceId}/grants with this key's `keyId` to actually let it do something.

201.description: Created - save `key` now, it will not be shown again

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

get.summary: List everything a key has been granted
get.description: Every DeviceGrant scoping this key to a device or project, across your whole account - the reverse view of a device's own Permissions tab, for seeing (and eventually managing) a single key's whole reach in one place.

post.summary: Register a webhook
post.description: Delivers every event type (relay_changed, telemetry, device_online/offline, schedule_fired) to `url`, scoped to whatever `keyId` already has a DeviceGrant for - no separate scope to configure. `keyId` is not a secret - it's the same value [List your account's API keys](/docs/reference/api-keys/list-your-accounts-api-keys) returns for each key (e.g. `key_9f8e7d6c`), not the key's raw secret value. No key yet? [Create an API key](/docs/reference/api-keys/create-an-api-key) first, then grant it device access before a webhook on it will deliver anything - see [Create a Scoped Device Grant](/docs/guides/create-a-scoped-device-grant). See [Receiving Webhooks](/docs/reference/receiving-webhooks) for how to receive and verify what gets delivered here. The signing secret is returned once, at creation only, and cannot be recovered afterward - rotate it with POST /:webhookId/rotate-secret if it's lost.

201.description: Created - save `secret` now, it will not be shown again

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

patch.summary: Update a webhook's URL or enabled state

post.summary: Rotate a webhook's signing secret
post.description: The previous secret stops verifying signatures immediately - update your endpoint's verification key before or right after calling this.

200.description: OK - save `secret` now, it will not be shown again

get.summary: Read a webhook's recent delivery attempts
get.description: The last 50 attempts, newest first - each event fires its own delivery row per attempt, so a retried delivery shows up multiple times with increasing `attempt`.

get.summary: List recent events across your whole account
get.description: A paginated audit log across every device you own - device online/offline, commands sent, unauthorized attempts, schedule changes. Use `cursor` from a previous response to page further back.

get.summary: List a single device's audit log
get.description: Same event log as GET /events, scoped to one device. Use `before` (an event id from a previous response) to page further back.

get.summary: List pending and past command approvals
get.description: A command marked `requiresApproval` on its CommandDefinition never executes immediately for a non-owner caller (including an API key) it lands here instead, waiting for an Owner/Admin to approve or deny it.

post.summary: Approve a pending command

200.description: OK the command is sent to the device immediately

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it

post.summary: Deny a pending command

get.summary: List the sub-devices connected behind this device
get.description: A device can act as an orchestrator ("master") for other physical devices connected to it locally (Bluetooth, WiFi) rather than directly to Nexalware - this lists everything reported behind it. Empty until the master actually reports a sub-device, see the [Device Orchestration](/docs/device-orchestration) docs for how a master does that. See [Receiving Webhooks](/docs/reference/receiving-webhooks) for the equivalent live-event story, sub-device events ride the same WebSocket feed and webhook pipeline device events already use.

schema.description: Only return readings for this metric name, omit to get every metric this sub-device reports.
Max rows to return, 1-1000. Defaults to 100.
Unix milliseconds - only return readings recorded at or after this time.

patch.description: Disabling a sub-device stops the master from accepting further commands for it (any `command`/`command/on`/`command/off` request targeting a disabled sub-device 404s), it does not remove it - state, telemetry history and its declared capabilities stay intact and it can be re-enabled at any time. Requires the same grant a command against this sub-device would need. Body is optional - omit it to flip the current state, or pass `enabled` explicitly.

enabled.description: Explicit target state. Omit to flip the current state.

403.description: Not permitted - see `message` for the specific reason and how to fix it
